The selected sequence is:

1. Make stop/cleanup results accurate and keep late results from changing a newer session.
2. Separate remembered identity from current presence and address ownership. Avoid treating a missed scan as proof of departure.
3. Add versioned events, reconnect snapshots and bounded local history with read-only replay.
4. Correct observed traffic direction and expose capture health and visibility limits.
5. Apply evidence expiry and use consistent names, icons and state labels across screens.
6. Evaluate any wider protocol coverage behind an independent feasibility and authorized-lab gate.
7. Review installation as a compatible app/helper pair and publish a measured support matrix.

The architecture remains SwiftUI plus a native Swift/C helper authenticated through XPC. Router credentials, endpoint enrollment and extra hardware are outside this direction. Dormant packet modules remain disabled until their own correctness and safety requirements are met. Automatic wireless disruption, exploit fallbacks and evasion of network protections are outside scope.

For a proposal, identify the concrete problem, affected component, smallest useful change, offline regression and remaining live uncertainty. A dependency needs licensing and packaging review; a package README is not compatibility evidence.
